svg.title: Event execution pipeline stages for an Update of a Cedar work order
svg.desc: A caller sends an Update for work order WO-1002. The request passes PreValidation (stage 10), which runs before security checks and usually outside the database transaction. Inside the database transaction it passes PreOperation (stage 20), MainOperation (stage 30, the platform writes the row) and PostOperation (stage 40). After PostOperation the transaction commits and the response returns to the caller. Asynchronous PostOperation steps are queued as system jobs and run after the commit. Cedar uses PreValidation to reject a past Scheduled for value, PreOperation to normalise the FieldLink ID in the Target, synchronous PostOperation to create a reschedule note in the same transaction, and an asynchronous PostOperation probe that cannot roll back the save.
svg.text: One message, four stages: Update of cedar_workorder (WO-1002)
system job runs after the commit
What Cedar registers on each stage (WorkOrderGuardPlugin, C-09 v0.1)
Reject Scheduled for in the past (AC1). Throwing here cancels before the transaction: nothing to roll back.
Trim and upper-case FieldLink ID inside the Target (AC2). The platform writes the corrected value: no second Update.
Create the reschedule note with the Organization service (AC3). Same transaction: both commit or neither does.
Runs later as a system job. If it fails, the job is marked Failed; the saved work order stays saved.
Rule: an exception in any synchronous step inside the transaction rolls back the whole operation.
